title: Recovery and Wind-Down Planning
summary: Why supervisors expect firms to plan for severe stress and orderly exit, and how the board tests that recovery options and wind-down plans would work in practice.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Why supervisors expect firms to plan for severe stress and orderly exit, and how the board tests that recovery options and wind-down plans would work in practice.
Learning Objectives: Explain the purpose of recovery plans and solvent wind-down planning
Assess recovery indicators, options and their feasibility
Evaluate whether the firm could wind down in an orderly way
Syllabus: Recovery indicators, triggers and escalation to the board
Recovery options: capital, liquidity, disposals and cost actions
Wind-down costs, timelines and client asset return
Testing plans through fire drills and playbooks
Intended Audience: Chairs, non-executive and independent directors and members of board risk and audit committees
Chief executives, finance and risk directors and senior managers accountable for strategy and planning
Company secretaries, strategy and planning teams supporting the board
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board or senior management experience in financial services is helpful. No specialist background in finance or risk modelling is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Principles for an Effective Risk Appetite Framework (2013)
Basel Committee, Corporate Governance Principles for Banks (2015)
